atoms.b:
Dystopia
A dystopia is a fictional society that represents a pessimistic and oppressive future. Dystopias are characterised by ((surveillance)) states, censorship, social ((inequality)) and oppression, while ((freedom)) and individuality are ((restricted)).

Utopia
A utopia is an ideal ((society)) that is unfortunately ((unattainable)) in reality. It refers to visions or dreams of a ((better)) future.

instruction.text: Decide whether the novels are utopias or dystopias.
instruction.sound: Decide whether the novels are utopias or dystopias.

atoms.a:
Utopia – Thomas More (1516)

This novel describes an island society where all property is shared, education is highly valued and people live peacefully and cooperatively. Poverty and crime are rare, and citizens are encouraged to contribute to the common good.

feedback.end: Thomas More's Utopia (1516) first introduced the word utopia. It is considered the first work of the utopian genre and has influenced many later works of literature.

atoms.a:
1984 – George Orwell (1949)

In a future version of Great Britain, citizens live under a totalitarian one-party government that constantly monitors their actions, controls information and punishes independent thinking. Propaganda, censorship and surveillance are used to maintain the Party's power over society.

The Hunger Games – Suzanne Collins (2008)

Set in Panem, a country built on the ruins of North America, society is divided into the wealthy Capitol and the poor districts. To remind citizens of the government's power, children are forced to participate in a televised competition where only one contestant can survive.

Fahrenheit 451 – Ray Bradbury (1953)

Set in a future American city, the novel describes a society where books are illegal and firefighters burn them whenever they are found. Citizens are encouraged to focus on entertainment rather than questioning the world around them.

Island – Aldous Huxley (1962)

Set on the fictional island of Pala, the novel portrays a society that values scientific knowledge, environmental awareness and spiritual well-being. Citizens are educated to think critically and live meaningful lives.

The Handmaid's Tale – Margaret Atwood (1985)

Set in a religious regime, the novel portrays a society in which women have lost many of their basic rights, including the right to work or read. Some women, called Handmaids, are deprived of their individuality and only valued in terms of their reproductive function. The regime forces them to have children for powerful families.

instruction.text: Decide whether the novels are utopian or dystopian. Some characteristics can appear in both genres.

feedback.end:
In utopias, genetic engineering may be used to prevent disease and improve health for everyone.
In dystopias, it often creates inequality by deciding people's abilities, looks, or social status before they are born.

Mandatory education can appear in both utopias and dystopias because education can empower people or control them.
In utopias, it ensures that everyone has equal access to education.
In dystopias, education is used to spread government propaganda and discourage independent thinking.
